correctness.rationale: At first bias-corrected step from zero moments, mhat=g and vhat=g^2 for any beta1,beta2 in (0,1), so r_i=g_i/(|g_i|+epsilon). LAMB scales -r by a positive factor; x^+ norm squared difference is -2a x.r+a^2||r||^2. The SPD turn-angle bound cos(angle(x,Hx))>=2 sqrt(kappa)/(kappa+1) follows by endpoint chord lambda^2<=(kappa+1)lambda-kappa and optimization of mean. In 2D, if x.g>0 but x.Teps(g)<=0 then angle(x,g)>pi/4: reflect x to quadrant I and examine the compression of a mixed-sign g's coordinate ratio toward one. Therefore kappa<=3+2sqrt2 ensures x.r>0 for every epsilon>0. For larger kappa the rotated two-eigenvalue maximizer makes x1>x2>0 and g1<0<g2 so x.sign(g)<0; scaling Hessian with fixed kappa makes r tend to sign(g). Independently checked rotated numerical witnesses above threshold and positivity of x.g, plus the explicit rational H,x example. This controls Euclidean distance, NOT objective descent; g.r always positive.
